title: Investigating the impact of Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) on Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety symptoms in female victims of domestic violence.

relevance.population: Women described as victims of domestic violence.
relevance.exposureEvidence: Women described as victims of domestic violence.
relevance.rationale: Explicit domestic/intimate-partner violence exposure in the studied population; psychological intervention is within Language scope.
relevance.transferLimit: See limitation and quality fields; no population-wide clinical recommendation is implied.

sampleSize.description: Full text resolves sample count: 62 randomized, 60 analyzed (28 intervention,32 control).

intervention.dose: Twelve 90-minute sessions, twice weekly in groups of three to five.
intervention.provider: Midwifery counselling master’s student with training certificate.

outcomes.name: PTSD, depression and anxiety
outcomes.result: Full-text narrative reports differences including anxiety, contrary to abstract anxiety claim.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence interval included when stated; otherwise not established from accessed source.

outcomes.name: Domestic violence

outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence interval included when stated; otherwise not established from accessed source.

finding: Full-text results report PTSD, depression and anxiety differences, while later violence difference is nonsignificant; these conflict with the abstract’s anxiety and violence claims.
limitation: Sample-count discrepancy resolves as attrition, but abstract versus full-text outcome contradictions remain. Severe symptoms excluded and analysis omitted two nonattenders.

design.randomizationEvidence: Open-label trial using a random-number table: 30 intervention and 32 control; two intervention nonattenders excluded.

quality.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.
quality.transferLimits: Generalizability is limited to the stated population, setting and comparator.

title: EMDR for Survivors of Sexual and Intimate Partner Violence at a Nonprofit Counseling Agency
journal: Journal of EMDR Practice and Research

relevance.population: Women with sexual-violence or IPV trauma
relevance.exposureEvidence: Publisher-deposited abstract explicitly identifies sexual violence or IPV.
relevance.rationale: Directly relevant clinical EMDR evidence for the target population.
relevance.transferLimit: Pooled sample; no isolated IPV effect established.

sampleSize.description: 41 women in a mixed-methods agency evaluation.

comparator: Pretreatment baseline; no concurrent control established.
finding: Depression, anxiety and PTSD decreased after treatment; interviews reported functional and self-perception changes.
limitation: No controlled effect; publication-year metadata conflict and cohort overlap need resolution.

design.randomizationEvidence: No random allocation described in abstract.
design.crossRationale: No cross: randomized design not established.

quality.confounding: Time, expectancy and agency care; earlier cohort overlap unresolved.
quality.transferLimits: Adult clinical samples do not establish benefit for children or violence prevention.
